verified_key_information_units.information: Segment performance: Estonia-Finland route revenue increased EUR 1.7 million to EUR 314.5 million (passenger volumes up 1.8%) while Finland-Sweden routes declined EUR 3.3 million to EUR 225.5 million (due to maintenance) and Estonia-Sweden routes fell EUR 12.1 million to EUR 85.3 million (passenger volumes down 12.5%).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Sales and Segments' section breaking down revenue and results by route, including passenger/cargo unit changes and maintenance impacts.

candidate_sentences.text: Estonia-Finland passenger numbers increased 1.8% and revenue rose to EUR 314.5 million, but the segment result declined by EUR 10.9 million to EUR 70.4 million.
Finland-Sweden revenue decreased to EUR 225.5 million and the segment result fell to EUR 1.3 million, partly reflecting 68 days of maintenance on two vessels.
Estonia-Sweden revenue dropped EUR 12.1 million to EUR 85.3 million, although its loss narrowed to EUR 1.2 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Net debt decreased to EUR 432.4 million (from EUR 537.7 million in 2024) with a net debt/EBITDA ratio of 3.3 (vs 3.1 in 2024); cash position impacted by EUR 44.6 million dividends paid (plus EUR 11.3 million related income tax) and EUR 113.5 million in loan repayments and interest during the year.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Liquidity and Cash Flow' section detailing net debt, dividend payments, and financing activities.

candidate_sentences.text: Interest-bearing liabilities declined 19.9% to EUR 445.9 million and net debt fell to EUR 432.4 million, despite the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio increasing to 3.3.

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital investments totaled EUR 33.0 million (focused on vessel maintenance and IT systems), with planned maintenance and repair works amounting to 73 vessel-days.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Liquidity and Cash Flow' and 'Investments and Vessels' sections specifying capital expenditures and maintenance days.

candidate_sentences.text: Capital expenditure increased to EUR 33.0 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic focus on emissions reduction includes preparations to transition shuttle vessels (MyStar and Megastar) to liquified biomethane from 2026, targeting a 75% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and cost mitigation amid regulatory pressures.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO Letter to Shareholders and Sustainability Strategy and Governance section outlining biofuel transition plans and environmental targets.

verified_key_information_units.information: Post-reporting-period management changes: Paavo Nõgene resigned as Chairman of the Management Board effective May 2026; Peep Jalakas appointed as new Chairman effective April 2026; Margus Schults removed from Management Board effective February 2026 (remaining as Managing Director of Tallink Silja Oy).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Note 25: 'Subsequent Events' and Management Report 'Events After the Reporting Period' detailing management board resignations and elections.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K5, K6, and K7 are PRESENT with clear coverage in the candidate. K4 (fleet management details) is MISSING—no mention of vessel sales, lay-up reductions, or chartered vessels. K8 (emissions reduction strategy) is MISSING—no reference to biomethane transition or emission targets. K9 (management changes) is MISSING—no post-reporting-period personnel updates. The summary captures most HIGH and MEDIUM importance financial and operational trends, but lacks three MEDIUM items, resulting in a Generally yes rating.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements logically follow one another without contradictions. The summary begins with overall performance trends, then breaks down financial metrics, followed by operational drivers, segment performance, cost factors, cash flow, capital structure, and liquidity. The relationships between metrics (revenue -> gross profit -> EBITDA -> EBIT -> net profit) are presented in a logical sequence. Segment results are explained with specific operational factors. There are no material repetitions, and the organization flows naturally from consolidated performance to detailed drivers. The arithmetic differences between segment figures and consolidated totals are not presented as exhaustive additive components, so they do not constitute contradictions under the evaluation rules.
